title: Skeuomorphism
body:
**Skeuomorphism** is design that imitates the appearance of a physical object, including
details that served a purpose in the original and serve none in the copy. A note-taking
application rendered as a leather-bound pad with stitched edges is the standard example.

Its purpose was to make an unfamiliar medium legible by borrowing a familiar appearance, which
is [[Interface Metaphor]] carried into the visual layer. It worked for a generation of
users meeting a graphical interface for the first time.

Flat design is the reaction, discarding the imitation and relying on layout, colour and
typography. It removed visual noise, and its failure mode is removing so much difference that a
[[Signifier]] disappears with it, leaving a screen where nothing indicates what can be pressed.

The save icon is the case worth keeping. It depicts a 3.5-inch floppy disk, an object most
current users have never handled, and it still works, because it stopped being a picture of
something and became a learned symbol. That is the fate of every successful metaphor, and it is
why arguments about whether an icon still resembles its original object usually miss the
question, which is whether users recognise it.
